sections.name: Revenant
sections.card:
Summary: A jetpack demon that flies and fires salvos of guided missiles from its rocket launchers. Its only other attack is a weaker claw swipe.
Weak points: Shoot off its rocket launchers and the missile attack is gone. It is left with a weak claw swipe and has to stay on the ground.
Looks like: Glowing green eyes, no blood on the forehead, fresh cybernetics at the head and neck, and cleaner-looking metal. Its rocket launchers have details that make them look like demonic mouths.
Tips: A dash or a double jump breaks its missile lock-on. It can dash too, to get out of the way of your fire.

sections.name: Mancubus
sections.card:
Summary: A big, slow heavy demon with arm cannons that throw fireballs from range. Up close it uses flamethrowers and a ground attack that leaves damaging energy on the floor. It has 3,500 health, or 490 while staggered.
Weak points: Shoot its arm cannons: damaged cannons make its attacks much weaker and switch the flamethrowers off completely. A chainsaw or glory kill on its chest makes it blow up, which hurts and staggers large demons nearby and can kill smaller ones.
Looks like: Two small, greenish eyes, and in its chest an exposed yellow organ like a heart that glows. Armour plating has replaced its original shell.
Tips: Fight it from range with heavy hitters. The rocket launcher works because it is too slow to dodge rockets, and the ballista takes its cannons off from far away. The heavy cannon's precision bolt also removes cannons from across an arena, but watch your back while scoped in. Do not let it corner you: its close-range damage is large.

sections.name: Pinky
sections.card:
Summary: A heavily armoured demon whose main attack is a charge. It has 1,000 health, and takes extra damage on its tail or from a blood punch.
Weak points: The tail has no armour, so attack it from behind for the most damage. One direct blood punch kills it outright, even head-on.
Looks like: Heavy armour covers its front and none covers its tail.
Tips: Dodge the charge with a double jump or a dash, and try to make it charge into a wall: that stuns it long enough to hit the tail. An ice bomb freezes it so it cannot turn round. Steady fire wears its front armour down, and the strongest weapons, like the ballista's destroyer blade mod, go straight through it.

sections.name: Baron of Hell
sections.card:
Summary: A tough demon carrying two flaming blades. It is fast and aggressive, and it can survive a direct hit from the BFG.
Looks like: Its skin is an ashy grey-brown, its eyes burn, the flesh inside glows like embers, and its blood is magma. It carries two flaming blades, and its projectiles are orange and red.
Tips: Stay at a distance, just outside its leaping reach, and swap quickly between your heaviest weapons: the ballista, rocket launcher and super shotgun work well. A blood punch knocks it back and makes it easier to stun, and steady chaingun fire can stall its attacks.

sections.name: Dread knight
sections.card:
Summary: A cybernetic Hell knight with an energy blade on each arm. Its arm blades extend its melee reach beyond a Hell knight's, it can throw an energy wave from a distance, and it has more health, but every trick that works on a Hell knight works on it too.
Looks like: A Hell knight with cybernetic upgrades and an energy blade fixed to each arm.
Tips: It crosses its arms before it throws its energy wave, so you can see it coming and dodge. Its leaping slam leaves a zone of damaging energy around itself, so stay back. Fire the rocket launcher's lock-on burst once to stagger it; the ballista and super shotgun make it flinch, and swapping between them stops it attacking at all.

sections.name: Prowler
sections.card:
Summary: A stealthy purple demon that teleports behind or beside you and then leaps in for a fast melee hit that does a lot of damage. It has 1,000 health, or 250 while staggered.
Weak points: A direct hit from the ballista staggers it at once, and the super shotgun kills it outright at point-blank range. An ice bomb holds it in place so it cannot teleport away.
Looks like: Like an imp but bigger, with long claws, purple skin and bony plates jutting from its back. Three eyes sit together in the middle of its face, and its jaw has three parts.
Tips: It is most dangerous in a group of other demons, because they keep you busy while it sets up its ambush. When it feels in danger it teleports away and tries another surprise attack. As it rushes in from far away it may shoot quick purple energy bolts.

sections.name: Carcass
sections.card:
Summary: A cyborg demon that fires ring-shaped lasers, makes shockwaves along the ground and puts up force fields to protect itself and other demons. It is fairly fragile, with 1,200 health, or 240 while staggered.
Weak points: Its force field resists explosives, but the plasma rifle or a blood punch destroys it easily. Shoot the round mark on the tank it carries on its back and it dies at once.
Looks like: A zombie human's upper body joined to a robot frame with three insect-like legs, a blaster in its right arm and a dish on its waist.
Tips: It often puts its shield in front of staggered demons, so you cannot glory kill them easily, or when you hold the rocket launcher or sticky bombs. If the shield is close to the carcass, pop it with the plasma rifle; if not, a couple of shots from the ballista or blasts from the super shotgun should be enough. Up close it does a spinning strike with two hits in a row.

sections.name: Pain elemental
sections.card:
Summary: A flying demon that makes lost souls and uses them as attacks: spat out as fast homing shots, thrown down as mines, or fired three at a time. Its health is roughly that of a baron of Hell.
Weak points: The rocket launcher's lock-on burst mod works well because it cannot dodge the guided missiles; two clear volleys kill it. Like other flying demons, it also takes bonus damage from the ballista.
Looks like: A round, flying, brown demon with one big red eye, a pair of long black horns, muscular arms with big claws and a large mouth with eight mandibles.
Tips: It air-dashes away when it sees a weapon pointed at it, so wait until it is busy with something else or just about to attack. It can push its lost souls into your shots as living shields. Thrown lost souls hit harder than a direct attack, and their splash damage makes tight spaces risky. Skip the meat hook: it may catch a lost soul and leave you in a dangerous spot.

sections.name: Tyrant
sections.card:
Summary: A cybernetic demon, the next step on from the classic cyberdemon, that fires missiles from an arm cannon. It comes back as a major enemy, often in pairs in later levels, and it survives one direct BFG hit.
Weak points: It turns slowly and its dash is poor, so the meat hook and super shotgun work as long as you stay behind it. The Crucible kills it in one hit.
Looks like: A two-legged demon built like the classic cyberdemon: gored belly with exposed ribs and tubing, a weapon in place of its left arm, an energy blade on its right arm, a pair of big horns at each side of the head, and yellowish-white eyes.
Tips: If it cannot see you it launches a missile barrage, and glowing runes mark where the missiles land. When it does see you it takes a moment to aim, so attack then. Its laser cannon is announced by a triple beep: duck behind cover, or dash right at the end so its aim is ruined. Up close it slashes with its blade or sends out shockwaves.

sections.name: Ballista
sections.card:
Summary: A heavy beam weapon that hits harder per shot than any other weapon before mods, with unmatched accuracy and a slow fire rate. You can get it once you are back from Doom Hunter Base.
Uses: The beam goes straight through lined-up fodder demons when it kills them. Each shot uses 25 cells, so save it for weak points that are too far away to reach with the heavy cannon or sticky bombs, for a hot-swap combo with another weapon, or for airborne enemies like the pain elemental, which takes bonus damage from it.
Tips: Two mods: Arbalest charges a dart that sticks in an enemy and blows up shortly after, but slows you down and needs a reload between shots. Destroyer Blade, after charging, fires a wide horizontal shot that pierces clustered enemies and uses 50 cells. The recoil can be used to gain air time and push yourself across an arena, and a full load with all ammo upgrades is only ten shots.

sections.name: Heavy cannon
sections.card:
Summary: An all-purpose automatic rifle with two mods, Precision Bolt and Micro Missiles. You get it early: after the second demon fight of the Hell on Earth level.
Uses: Reliable from a medium or long distance, and two body shots are enough for most fodder. On its own it is weaker against strong enemies, so use it to back up other weapons from a distance. The Precision Bolt scope adds extra damage on weak points, enough to destroy an arachnotron's cannon or a revenant's rocket launchers. Micro Missiles give area damage without the risk to yourself that the rocket launcher carries when used up close.
Tips: For Maykr drones the Precision Bolt is the mod to pick, because a headshot makes them drop a lot of resources. The cannon is hitscan, so a shot hits or misses the moment it is fired, which suits fast fodder at long range that the plasma rifle cannot hit. The micro missiles home in a little, and you must reload between salvos of up to six.

sections.name: Plasma rifle
sections.card:
Summary: A rapid-fire energy rifle that shoots small, bright blue orbs of plasma. You first meet it in Exultia, after the trans-dimensional portal.
Uses: Energy shields, like those of the shield soldier and the carcass, overload and explode under plasma fire, hurting their owner and nearby enemies. It can also switch off the body shield of a Doom hunter and chip at an armoured baron's armour. The arch-vile and the marauder use magical shields that it cannot touch.
Tips: Enemies hit by several orbs in a short time burst in an energy blast, which helps against groups but can spoil a glory kill. The Microwave Beam mod locks onto an enemy and holds it still while it takes constant damage, and it is the only weapon you have that can kill a spirit, so keep it stocked against a possessed demon. Heat Blast fires a cone in front of the weapon, and you charge it up by shooting normally.

sections.name: Ice bomb
sections.card:
Summary: A bomb launched from the Praetor suit's shoulder launcher that flash-freezes its target. The frozen enemy cannot move and shatters once it has taken enough damage. You pick it instead of the frag grenade with a toggle.
Uses: Use it to hold a target while you attack it, to stop a dangerous enemy fighting back, or to escape when you are surrounded. It is strongly recommended against whiplashes, and it holds a pinky or spectre still so you can hit the weak rear. Frozen enemies cannot be glory killed.
Tips: Freeze time depends on the enemy: 4 seconds for fodder, 2 for pinkies, revenants and cacodemons, 1.5 for mancubi and barons of Hell, and 1 for tyrants, with longer times once upgraded. Demons that a spirit has possessed or a screecher has buffed are immune. The cooldown is 45 seconds, or 35 with the faster cooldown suit upgrade.

sections.name: Flame belch
sections.card:
Summary: A brief jet of fire from the Praetor suit's shoulder launcher that sets enemies ablaze. You find it at the Fortress of Doom once Hell on Earth is done, and it is always ready on top of whichever grenade type you picked.
Uses: Burning enemies take extra damage and drop armour shards, and killing one while it burns drops a larger pile. It is the main source of armour in a fight, one part of the combat loop, next to the chainsaw and glory kills. Turn left and right as you fire to hit a group.
Tips: The combat shotgun and super shotgun give more armour when they kill a burning enemy. The cooldown is 25 seconds, or 12.5 with the Quickdraw Belch upgrade. Sentinel crystals unlock three upgrades: the quicker cooldown, longer burning on the heaviest demons, and faster armour drops.

sections.name: Blood punch
sections.card:
Summary: A strong melee attack that you charge up with glory kills. Its shockwave also hurts foes near the one you hit. You first find it as a glowing artifact in Exultia.
Uses: It kills pinkies and spectres instantly, or at least badly hurts them, and does big damage to tougher demons. It breaks through enemy shields, even the arch-vile's magic one, and very often hits weak points, even destroying the cyber-mancubus's armour completely.
Tips: It needs no ammo, but two glory kills give one charge and you can store only one at a time. Clearing Doom Hunter Base makes the shockwave stronger. After Sentinel Prime, one glory kill on a heavy demon fills it straight away, and after Urdak you can hold two charges. Against a group of fodder, freeze them, burn them with the flame belch, then blood punch one to refill health and armour.
